name: Elihu
overview: Elihu is a male figure identified as the son of Barachel who speaks to Job, as recorded in Job 32:2. There is no tribal affiliation or additional notes provided about him. His role is notable within the context of the Book of Job.
namesAndTitles: The name Elihu means 'y-h-v-h is [my] G-d,' reflecting a theologically significant declaration of God's identity. This proper name is not indicated as given directly by God but carries a meaningful connection to the divine name.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Elihu is the son of Barachel, as stated in Job 32:2. No other family relationships are documented beyond this.
scriptureSignificance: Elihu's significance lies in his role as a speaker to Job during a critical moment in the narrative. As the son of Barachel, he contributes to the theological discourse in the Book of Job, emphasizing God's sovereignty and justice. His presence adds depth to the dialogue surrounding suffering and divine purpose.
